headline.text: In Etelä-Pohjanmaa, the crude symptomatic treatment share of 28.1% (95% CI 24.5–32.1; n=152/540) is below the national 39.5% (5871/14873), as its 95% confidence interval excludes the national value.

details.text: Because treatment categories overlap, patients can receive several types: the crude curative treatment share is 30.6% (95% CI 26.8–34.6; n=165/540), whose 95% confidence interval includes the national 27.0% (4009/14873), while the crude life-prolonging treatment share is 40.4% (95% CI 36.3–44.6; n=218/540), whose 95% confidence interval excludes the national 30.4% (4522/14873).

The crude share with no treatment record within 12 months is 25.7% (95% CI 22.2–29.6; n=139/540), whose 95% confidence interval includes the national 27.5% (4089/14873), and this category mixes untreated patients and unrecorded treatment.

The crude share with a multidisciplinary team (MDT) meeting recorded is 32.4% (95% CI 28.6–36.5; n=175/540) versus 6.0% (893/14873) nationally, but MDT records measure recording practice, not care, because HILMO captures procedures only from direct patient contacts.

Public registry data do not report county waiting times, while preliminary, unpublished figures show lung cancer care in Finland takes 155 days on average from first symptoms to treatment (56 days patient delay, 41 days in primary care, and 58 days in specialist care), compared with 107 days in Sweden and 67 days in Denmark.

headline.text: County treatment shares are crude, unadjusted figures, and public registry data do not capture primary care, referrals, stage at diagnosis for about 48% of patients, or treatment start dates.

details.text: The county shares are crude and have separate limitations: they are not age-adjusted (digitised age-adjusted shares from Kuva 16, at ±0.5 percentage points precision, exist only for curative treatment by sex, with national lines at 26.7% for men and 26.9% for women), and they cannot be stage-adjusted because stage at diagnosis is missing for about 48% of patients.

According to a journal article, hospital discharge register (HILMO) diagnoses match the Cancer Registry for about 90% of most cancer types, but this concerns diagnosis concordance only, and 93.6% of patients have a specialist lung cancer visit in HILMO within 12 months without showing when the visit or treatment started.

Public report data do not measure symptom onset or referral dates, primary care visits are not included in the report's data, occupational health is not mentioned, and imaging appears only indirectly as diagnosis by clinical examination alone in about 20% of patients rather than imaging waits.

headline.text: The team recommends tracking access times with THL guidance Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions, standardising referrals and diagnostic coordination, and publishing county recording coverage for stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding.

details.text: Because the Health Care Act (§52) sets no legal maximum time for a cancer suspicion and Finland lacks a unified national monitoring system, the team recommends reporting county access times (referral to first specialist visit to diagnosis to treatment start) using THL guidance Ohjaus 21/2016 definitions for 16 cancers and flagging stalled handovers.

Since mentor insight indicates a weak referral gets a lower urgency rating, and the Filha programme's diagnostics recommendation with primary-care referral criteria and recommended time limits is to be carried out before the 2030 mid-term evaluation, the team recommends adopting a standard referral template, referring persistent symptoms after a normal X-ray, and naming a diagnostic contact person.

While the STM roadmap (measure 3.2.1) plans a national cancer quality registry alongside THL's Cancer Registry with the registry decree updated by 2026–2028 and 90% data coverage including stage by 2029–2031, the team recommends publishing per-county recording coverage for stage, drug treatment, and MDT coding and reading county gaps in these fields as data-quality signals first.

q:4e702a20fe.claim_text: Finland has no unified national system to steer the drafting of cancer-specific treatment recommendations, or the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care, and cancer-specific and generic PROMs). Existing recommendations and pathways, and the targets and indicators to be monitored, are not coordinated nationally. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.
q:4e702a20fe.quote: Suomessa ei ole yhtenäistä kansallista järjestelmää, joka ohjaisi syöpäkohtaisten hoitosuositusten laatimista sekä niihin perustuvien hoitoketjujen toteutusta ja seurantaa (laatu- ja vaikuttavuustavoitteet/indikaattorit, mukaan lukien hoitoonpääsy sekä syöpäkohtaiset ja geneeriset PROM-vointimittarit). Olemassa olevia hoitosuosituksia ja -ketjuja sekä seurattavia tavoitteita ja indikaattoreita ei koordinoida kansallisella tasolla. Tämä ylläpitää alueellista eriarvoisuutta syövän hoidon saatavuudessa ja vaikuttavuudessa.
q:4e702a20fe.quote_en: Finland does not have a uniform national system to guide the preparation of cancer-specific clinical guidelines and the implementation and monitoring of care pathways based on them (quality and effectiveness targets/indicators, including access to care as well as cancer-specific and generic PROM well-being measures). Existing clinical guidelines and care pathways as well as monitored targets and indicators are not coordinated at the national level. This maintains regional inequality in the availability and effectiveness of cancer care.

rec:1.claim_text: Team recommendation 1: Counties report access times using the THL 21/2016 definitions, with handover alerts. Each wellbeing services county reports lung cancer access times (referral → first specialist visit → diagnosis → treatment start) using the definitions in THL's Hoitoonpääsyn seuranta syövän hoidossa (Ohjaus 21/2016). Until national target times exist, flag stalled handovers.

rec:2.claim_text: Team recommendation 2: A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact. Adopt a standard referral content list and template, modelled on KYS. • Add a rule for primary care: if symptoms persist after a normal X-ray, refer for a pulmonologist assessment. • Name a contact person for the diagnostic phase, from referral to diagnosis.
rec:2.location: §2. A KYS-style referral template, a persistent-symptoms rule and a named contact
